name: Vanta Ordnance Railgun Pistol RP-1 'Thumbtack'
description:
A compact electromagnetic accelerator small enough to be carried and fired with one hand. The Thumbtack fires a 1.5mm tungsten needle at Mach 4 from a barrel just 12cm long, achieving penetration that rivals rifle-caliber kinetic weapons in a package the size of a large pistol.

Vanta Ordnance spent six years miniaturizing railgun technology to produce the RP-1. The weapon's capacitor bank occupies most of the grip, and the electromagnetic accelerator runs the full length of the weapon's upper assembly. The result is a pistol that weighs 2.1 kg loaded — heavy for a handgun, but transformative in terms of capability.

The Thumbtack's limitation is heat management. The compact design leaves no room for cooling systems, and the barrel temperature after three rapid shots is sufficient to cause thermal warping that degrades accuracy. Operators learn to fire slowly and deliberately, treating the rail pistol as a precision weapon rather than a rapid-fire sidearm.
legality: Licensed — restricted to registered operators with railgun authorization
specifications:
caliber: 1.5mm tungsten needle
effective_range: 10-200 meters
rate_of_fire: 1 round per 3 seconds (recommended), 1 per second (maximum, degrades barrel)
capacity: 12-round magazine
weight: 2.1 kg
power_source: Grip-integrated capacitor, 24 shots per charge
tactical_use: The Thumbtack is deployed as a concealable anti-armor sidearm. Its tungsten needle penetrates body armor that would stop conventional pistol rounds, giving the operator a backup weapon capable of defeating protected targets. The weapon is particularly valued by operators who work undercover or in environments where carrying a rifle is impractical. The RP-1's compact size allows it to be drawn and fired faster than any conventional anti-armor weapon.
cultural_context: The Thumbtack has become a prestige sidearm in GLMZ's operator community. Carrying a railgun in a pistol format signals both financial resources (the RP-1 costs more than most conventional rifles) and professional capability (the weapon's limited shots demand precision). Street-level criminals have begun seeking bootleg copies, but the manufacturing precision required for miniaturized railgun technology has so far defeated black-market fabrication attempts.
story_hooks: A Thumbtack has been used in three assassinations where the shooter was confirmed to be within arm's reach of the target. The 1.5mm entry wound was initially mistaken for a medical injection site. Someone is using the rail pistol as a contact-distance execution tool.

Vanta Ordnance's barrel manufacturing process has been stolen — the proprietary heat-resistant alloy that allows the RP-1's barrel to survive electromagnetic acceleration is now in the hands of a black-market fabricator who is producing knock-offs with inferior materials. The copies work for approximately 20 shots before the barrel fails catastrophically.
related_entities: Ringo Heavy Transit MagRail Levitation Transport Network

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist pistol with an oversized upper assembly that dwarfs its grip. The barrel section is chunky and angular, dominated by the visible electromagnetic accelerator rails running its length. Despite being 'compact,' it reads as purposeful and dense—a weapon built for lethality over ergonomics. The profile is asymmetrical: top-heavy with a pronounced rail housing, tapered grip.
physical_description.dimensions: Overall length 24cm, barrel 12cm, width at rail housing 3.2cm, grip diameter 2.8cm
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty and front-weighted. 2.1kg feels substantial in one hand, the mass concentrated forward of the trigger group. Balanced on a knife's edge between 'controllable' and 'unwieldy'—demands respect and two-handed shooting stance despite single-hand capability.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade polymer frame with integrated titanium rail housing. Capacitor bank occupies the grip interior, visible as layered metallic components through transparent grip sections.
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal polymer body with brushed titanium rail guides. Heat-stress discoloration visible along the barrel in well-used examples—oxidized blues and purples creeping from the muzzle back 4-5cm.
physical_description.color_scheme: Industrial gray-black primary with silver-titanium accelerator rails exposed. Capacitor components visible through grip translucency in deep metallic blue.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer with embedded heat-dissipation lattice pattern. Slight tackiness from capacitor thermal management. Finger grooves deliberately aggressive—built for control, not comfort.
distinctive_features: Exposed dual electromagnetic rails running full barrel length—primary visual signature
Translucent grip section revealing capacitor architecture beneath
Heat vents cut into upper rail housing as geometric patterns
Ammo counter LED on left side—small red/green indicator
Tungsten needle loading breach on top of rail assembly
Charging port on grip base (proprietary Vanta connector)
Wear rings around muzzle from barrel thermal stress
Faint grid-pattern etching from rail coil wrapping showing through finish
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: VANTA ORDNANCE in block letters stamped on left rail housing. Serial plate (brushed aluminum, 2cm x 0.8cm) mounted below charging port. RP-1 designation and railgun warning symbol (⚡ in circle) engraved above trigger guard.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field specimens show predictable heat-scarring on barrel. Capacitor housing invariably shows micro-scratches from repeated charging cycles. Professional operators maintain matte finish; some aftermarket grip wraps appear in grey or black. Thermal discoloration inevitable and considered a badge of proper use.
